database-tests.root_cause: The unchanged integrated lifecycle fixture creates default Solo and inserts a second active member, assuming the old two-seat default. The approved Solo expansion intentionally makes default Solo 1 one seat, independently verified by the task SQL; the exact trusted failure in verification 356 is the stale fixture precondition, not a broken member limit. The generic lifecycle/employee-authorization fixture now selects Team, retaining selected-family idempotence, seven-day trial, valid employee denial, negotiated quotes, immutable periods, downgrade blockers, retained history and suspension/reactivation assertions. Its later two-member Solo downgrade explicitly selects Solo 2. This correction advances past the observed fixture failure and deliberately leaves the real Solo 2 reactivation assertion intact; independent local probing reveals a subsequent product defect there, which requires a new trusted outcome before product retry accounting. Separately, the required task SQL is currently unrun and its JSON expected-values literal misses only the outer closing bracket. Restoring that bracket preserves all seven assertions; all seven pass in an independent local probe. That probe is not substituted for required verification. Neither unrun check nor future product outcome is classified as PASS or given a fabricated receipt.
